name: EVI INDUSTRIES INC

devils_advocate.strongest_counter: The verdict turns entirely on one input I chose, and the other choice is defensible. At the engine's pre-Sudsies enterprise value of $240.1M (market cap $195.9M plus $51.0M revolver less $6.774M cash), the market implies -6.0% growth on a three-year reported-FCFF mean, +0.2% on FY2026's reported FCFF, and +9.6% on FY2026's FCFF with stock comp expensed. A 16-point swing produced by the SBC treatment alone. If stock compensation is a genuine cost of retaining a distribution salesforce that is already reflected in the diluted share count, expensing it double-counts, and on the reported figures EVI is cheap rather than dear. The second counter is that I am charging EVI $37.4M for Sudsies while crediting it with zero of Sudsies' earnings, which is asymmetric — Sudsies consolidates from the quarter ending 2026-09-30 and if it was bought at a normal small-services multiple it adds several million of EBITDA against a $16M FCFF base.
devils_advocate.what_would_prove_it: FY2027 quarterly cash flow statements, specifically operating cash flow less capex less acquisition spend now that the acquisition line has fallen to $7.2M — a light acquisition year with rising free cash flow would show the annuity compounding underneath, which is the bull's whole claim. And the first disclosure of Sudsies revenue and EBITDA, which would let the $37.4M be judged.
devils_advocate.already_visible: Partly, and it argues for me. FY2026 was already a light acquisition year — $7.2M against $46.9M in FY2025 — and free cash flow still FELL, from $16.40M to $13.45M, because capex rose 47% and working capital consumed cash. The bull needs a year where EVI stops buying and the cash appears; FY2026 was close to that year and the cash did not appear. Against me: the record gross margin is real and rising, and capex below D&A means the fixed-asset base is not being starved.
devils_advocate.unresolved: I still cannot value Sudsies — EVI has now disclosed the price ($37.4M) twice and the economics never, and the 10-K says the purchase price allocation is incomplete, so even goodwill is unknown. I also cannot separate organic from acquired revenue: EVI gives no organic disclosure, and my inference that organic is roughly flat rests on the company's own attribution sentence plus flat operating margin, not on a disclosed figure.

what_changed: The FY2026 10-K (year ended 2026-06-30) was filed 2026-09-08 and is the document the 2026-09-03 devil's-advocate pass on this name explicitly nominated as the settling observable and could not obtain. It settles the question. FY2026: operating cash flow $20.606M (vs $21.265M), capital expenditures $7.152M (vs $4.861M), cash paid for acquisitions net of cash acquired $7.182M (vs $46.925M). The nominated test was 'full-year operating cash flow LESS both capex and cash paid for acquisitions': FY2026 = +$6.27M, FY2025 = -$30.52M, two-year sum -$24.25M. The prior pass said 'if it is persistently near zero or negative, my base case is right.' It is. Separately, CFO-less-capex fell to $13.45M from $16.40M and $27.8M in the two prior years — a monotonic three-year decline through what the company calls the strongest year in its history. Also new: Sudsies closed 2026-09-01 for a total purchase price of $37.4 million in cash (not the ~$34.6M previously estimated), against $6.774M of cash and a $51.0M revolver balance at year end, so it was debt-funded; EVI has still disclosed no revenue or EBITDA for Sudsies. Stock compensation was $5.298M in FY2026, 33% of reported FCFF.
consensus_case: EVI is a $446.6M-revenue value-added distributor of commercial laundry equipment that has compounded revenue for a decade by buying small private distributors. At $15.22 the market caps it at $195.9M, roughly 12.7x the FY2026 free cash flow it actually produced. The bear case the price embodies is simple and, on the FY2026 10-K filed 2026-09-08, correct: the revenue growth is bought, not earned. Management's own MD&A says the 15% revenue increase was 'primarily attributable to revenues generated by businesses acquired by the Company during fiscal 2025 and fiscal 2026.' Gross margin hit a record 31.5% and operating income rose 14%, yet SG&A grew 20% against revenue's 15%, operating margin was flat at 3.5%, net income rose only 3%, and diluted EPS FELL from $0.49 to $0.48. Free cash flow declined for the third consecutive year. The market is pricing a distributor whose scale grows and whose per-share economics do not.
base_case_rationale: I expense stock compensation: $5.3M on a founder-controlled microcap whose diluted share count is rising and whose diluted EPS fell while net income rose is real dilution, and the falling EPS is that dilution showing up. That puts FY2026 FCFF at $16.03M reported ($13.45M FCF plus $2.58M of after-tax interest) and $10.74M expensed, against $13.71M expensed in FY2025. I use a two-year expensed average of $12.2M rather than the engine's two-year window ending FY2025, because FY2024's pre-acquisition-heavy cash flow no longer describes this company. From there I underwrite +3% FCFF growth. The mechanisms that genuinely compound are the parts-and-service annuity and the record 31.5% gross margin, which is up 110bp on mix and 'solution selling'; the mechanisms that do not are the distribution business itself, where SG&A is growing faster than revenue and consuming the entire gross-margin gain, and interest expense, up 44%. Capex of $7.2M sits below D&A of $8.1M, so the company is not over-investing in fixed assets — the cash goes to acquisitions, which sit in investing activities where a CFO-less-capex definition never charges for them. +3% is real but modest: it credits the annuity and the margin, and refuses to credit growth that has to be bought.
key_risks: The +159% baseline gap is a roll-up artifact and should be disregarded entirely: the +10.6% revenue CAGR it applies to FCFF was bought with acquisition cash that never appears in CFO minus capex, and the FY2026 10-K has the company itself attributing the 15% revenue increase to acquired businesses

The verdict is not robust to the stock-compensation choice: expensing $5.298M moves the growth the market requires from +0.2% to +9.6%, i.e. from cheap to rich, and I have no basis stronger than judgment for preferring one
Free cash flow has fallen three years running ($27.8M, $16.40M, $13.45M) while revenue rose 15% and the company described fiscal 2026 as the strongest year in its history

$37.4M — 19% of market capitalisation — was deployed on 2026-09-01 into Sudsies, the first acquisition outside EVI's competence, with no disclosed revenue, EBITDA or purchase price allocation, funded on the revolver
Goodwill and intangibles are $122.8M of $304.5M of total assets; SG&A grew 20% against 15% revenue growth and operating margin was flat at 3.5%
$1.4M average daily dollar volume on a $196M company: this is not a liquid position
watch_for: FY2027 free cash flow in a year when acquisition spend stays near FY2026's $7.2M — the clean test of whether the underlying business generates cash when it is not buying
First disclosure of Sudsies revenue and EBITDA, and the completed purchase price allocation showing how much of the $37.4M became goodwill
Whether the SG&A growth rate falls back below the revenue growth rate, which is what the 'optimization initiatives' and growth spending being finite would look like
Whether the delayed installation backlog converts in FY2027 revenue or is described as delayed again
